The core content focuses on comparing two prevailing economic theories regarding government expenditure and economic growth: Keynesian economics and supply-side economics.

Similarities:
Both Keynesian and supply-side economics share the same ultimate goal: achieving economic growth. Despite their differing approaches, both theories are concerned with the mechanisms that drive a nation's economy forward.

Differences:
The primary difference lies in their methodology and the role assigned to the government versus the private sector. Keynesian economists argue for increased government spending as a means to stimulate the economy, particularly during downturns, positioning the government as the primary engine of growth. In contrast, supply-side economists contend that lower taxes and reduced government spending encourage private sector growth, thereby positioning the private sector as the primary driver of economic expansion.
